source: ដំណាំទុរេន (Durian Cultivation), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Department of Agricultural Extension, 2015, 31pp
text:
Land preparation should clear weeds and old vegetation, and where the water table is shallow, form raised planting mounds or beds to keep the root zone above standing water, matching the guidance also given in Source A of this batch. Planting holes should be dug generously sized (large enough to accommodate the root ball without cramping it) and enriched with compost or well-rotted manure mixed into the backfill soil.

Spacing recommendations depend on how the grower intends to manage the mature canopy: a wider spacing (matching roughly the 9m x 9m pattern given in Source A) suits a traditional large, spreading tree, while growers using more intensive pruning to keep trees smaller can plant more closely, but should be aware that crowding reduces air circulation through the canopy and raises disease pressure, particularly for the fungal diseases described in this batch that favor high humidity.
